name: abtn_receive_packet
prose: ADB receive callback for the hotkey device (adb_buttons.c:109-156, returns u_int, always 0 by its single return). It reads the first data byte (data[0] is read without checking len, so the caller must supply at least one byte) as cmd and switches on it: 0x0a sends a devctl 'brightness notify=down'; 0x09 sends 'brightness notify=up'; 0x08 and 0x01 send 'mute'; 0x07 and 0x02 send 'volume notify=down'; 0x06 and 0x03 send 'volume notify=up'; 0x0b sends 'eject'; 0x0c (mirror display) and 0x7f (numlock) do nothing; any other value does nothing unless DEBUG is defined, in which case a value with the high bit clear prints 'unknown ADB button 0x%x'. The status, command, reg and len arguments are not used. It returns 0 in all cases.
note: Reviewers: original right (devctl side effects, data[0] read regardless of len); round 15 right (the DEBUG print is only in the default case, so 0x0c and 0x7f are silent, 138-153).

name: adlink_ioctl
prose: Character device ioctl handler (adlink.c:193-360, returns int). It reads the argument u = *(u_int *)data (data is dereferenced for every command) and switches on cmd. SETDIVISOR returns EBUSY if running, EINVAL if u is odd, else stores the divisor. SETCHUNKSIZE returns EBUSY unless the state is RESET, EINVAL if u is not a multiple of PAGE_SIZE, and EINVAL if ringsize != 0 and ringsize % u is non-zero; for u == 0 the test 'u % PAGE_SIZE' passes and 'ringsize % u' with a non-zero ringsize divides by zero (not guarded); otherwise it stores chunksize. SETRINGSIZE returns EBUSY unless RESET, EINVAL if u is not page-multiple or chunksize != 0 and u % chunksize is non-zero, else stores ringsize. START returns EBUSY if running; if the state is RESET it applies defaults (chunksize 4 pages, ringsize 16 chunks, divisor 4), computes nchunks and returns EINVAL if nchunks is 0 or if the generation array plus the page-0 header would not fit in one page (nchunks * sizeof(sample) + sizeof(*p0) > PAGE_SIZE); it then allocates the chunk descriptor array (M_WAITOK) and a contiguous buffer for each chunk, linking them in a ring. For any state other than RUN it clears all sample generation words, programs the device registers, sets the state to RUN, loads the first chunk address and size and starts the hardware, then returns 0. STOP does nothing if the state is RESET, otherwise sets state = EINTR and sleeps in a loop (tsleep) until the generation word of the next chunk becomes non-zero. Any other command returns ENOIOCTL. So the possible returns are 0, EBUSY, EINVAL and ENOIOCTL (plus the possible trap on the zero divisor).
note: Reviewers: original right (EINVAL when the generation array plus page 0 exceeds PAGE_SIZE, 260-262); round 15 right (SETCHUNKSIZE with u == 0 and a non-zero ringsize divides by zero, 215-218). The tsleep loop in STOP has no timeout and is not interruptible by return value handling.

name: ahci_timeout
prose: Callout handler for a command timeout on one AHCI slot (ahci.c:1856-1932, void). It returns at once if the slot is below AHCI_SLOT_RUNNING. If the slot is RUNNING but not yet EXECUTING it reads the port's SACT and current command slot: if the slot's bit is set in SACT, or it is the current command slot, or FBS is enabled, or wrongccs is already set, it marks the slot EXECUTING; else if the current slot is not one of our running slots it sets ch->wrongccs and marks it EXECUTING; then it re-arms the callout for half of the ccb timeout (ahci_timeout again) and returns. Otherwise (a real timeout) it prints diagnostics. If a frozen ccb exists it takes it, sets its status to CAM_REQUEUE_REQ | CAM_RELEASE_SIMQ (this assignment overwrites any earlier status bits), then, because CAM_DEV_QFRZN is never set at that point, it always freezes the device queue and sets CAM_DEV_QFRZN, and completes the ccb with ahci_done (so the queue freeze is unconditional, not conditional on the old status). Then if FBS is not enabled and wrongccs is not set it takes the single-command path: it sets fatalerr, ends the timed-out slot's transaction with AHCI_ERR_TIMEOUT and ends every other running slot with AHCI_ERR_INNOCENT; otherwise (FBS enabled, or wrongccs set even without FBS) it freezes the SIM queue the first time, adds the slot to toslots, calls ahci_process_timeout if no other running slots remain outside toslots, else prints that it is waiting for the remaining slots (the slot is not ended immediately on this path).
note: Reviewers: original right (a non-FBS channel with wrongccs takes the FBS-style path, 1909, and the slot is not ended immediately); round 15 right (the CAM_DEV_QFRZN test at 1903 is always true after the status assignment at 1902).

name: ahd_handle_scsiint
prose: SCSI interrupt handler for the AIC79xx (aic79xx.c:1523-1792, void; the slice cut the head). It selects SCSI mode, reads SSTAT0/1/3, LQISTAT1, LQOSTAT0 and SSTAT2, masks the selection bits with SIMODE0, finds the current SCB (NULL if the sequencer reports NOT_IDENTIFIED), then handles exactly one condition in this priority order (an else-if chain): IOERR (transceiver mode change: clears it, resets channel A, re-runs the iocell workaround with pause/unpause); OVERRUN (message, correctable-error accounting, channel reset); SCSIRSTI (message, reset channel without initiating, uncorrectable-error accounting); SCSIPERR (clears the critical section, ahd_handle_transmission_error); lqostat0 non-zero (prints it and only clears the LQO interrupt bits, with no pause/unpause or restart); SELTO (stops selection, clears message and interrupt state, finds the waiting SCB, marks it CAM_SEL_TIMEOUT and runs ahd_handle_devreset, or reports an uncorrectable error if there is no SCB; then clears the SCSI interrupt, re-initialises the iocell and unpauses); SELDI/SELDO (iocell first selection, unpause); status3 non-zero (prints a cell parity error, counts a correctable error with AHD_CORRECTABLE_ERROR, and clears the status bits, with no unpause); LQI phase errors (clear critical section, ahd_handle_lqiphase_error); LQICRCI_NLQ (only clears that interrupt bit); BUSFREE or LQOBUSFREE (clears selection, decides whether the busfree was packetized, calls ahd_handle_pkt_busfree or ahd_handle_nonpkt_busfree, clears the busfree status, optionally the FIFO and message state and the SCSI interrupt, then restarts the sequencer if the handler said so, else unpauses); if none of the conditions matches it prints 'Missing case', dumps the card state, clears the interrupt status and unpauses. Only some branches restart, reset or unpause the controller; the lqostat0, status3 and LQICRCI_NLQ branches only clear status.
note: Slice cut the head. Reviewers: original right (the lqostat0, status3 and LQICRCI_NLQ branches only clear status, 1585-1589, 1654-1658, 1664-1671); round 15 right (the status3 branch also calls AHD_CORRECTABLE_ERROR, 1657). Callees not read.

name: ahd_handle_nonpkt_busfree
prose: Handles a non-packetized bus free (aic79xx.c:2164-2435, returns int; the slice cut the head). It reads the last phase and the saved SCSI id and LUN, builds the initiator devinfo, finds the current SCB (NULL if NOT_IDENTIFIED), and sets printerror = 1. If the last phase was MESGOUT it checks which message was just sent: an abort/abort-tag message aborts the SCB(s) (and returns 1 early, restarting the sequencer, when there is no SCB); a bus-device-reset message runs ahd_handle_devreset; a sent PPR, WDR or SDTR message reverts or applies transfer settings (ahd_set_width / ahd_set_syncrate) as appropriate; expected IDE or QAS-reject busfree flags are recognised; each handled case clears printerror. If printerror is still set, the last phase was a message phase and a PPR busfree was expected, it freezes the devq, marks the SCB CAM_REQUEUE_REQ and freezes it, then either aborts the SCBs of that target (when the IU requirement changed) or calls ahd_done(ahd, scb) on this SCB (so ahd_done can be called here), and clears printerror. If printerror is still set, it prints the unexpected-busfree report, aborts the SCBs for the target when an SCB was identified (CAM_UNEXP_BUSFREE), counts an uncorrectable error, dumps the card state and, unless the last phase was P_BUSFREE, forces renegotiation. The function has no return 0: every path, including the early one, returns 1 (restart the sequencer).
note: Slice cut the head. Reviewers: original right (there is no 'return 0': handled busfrees fall through to return 1, 2433-2434); round 15 WRONG: ahd_done is called on the PPR-negotiation busfree path (aic79xx.c:2396). Partly read: the per-message handling between 2198 and 2372 was skimmed. Callees not read.

name: ahd_init
prose: Initialises an AIC79xx controller (aic79xx.c:6225-6464, returns int; the slice is its middle and tail). It probes the stack size and mallocs saved_stack, returning ENOMEM if that fails. It then builds the DMA resources in stages, each stage incrementing ahd->init_level only after that stage succeeded: the buffer DMA tag (ENOMEM on failure, init_level unchanged), the shared-data tag (ENOMEM on failure), the shared-data memory allocation (ENOMEM on failure); after mapping the shared memory it sets up the queued hscb and increments init_level, and then ahd_init_scbdata is called AFTER that increment (so on its failure, which returns ENOMEM, init_level has already been counted for the previous stage). It then clears AHD_RESET_BUS_A if the initiator role is off, calls ahd_platform_init and ahd_chip_init, and, if AHD_CURRENT_SENSING is set, probes the termination current-sensing through the flexport registers; any timeout in that probe prints a message and jumps to init_done (it is not an error return). At init_done it calls ahd_restart, restarts the statistics timer and returns 0. So the only error returns are ENOMEM from the allocation steps; everything after ahd_init_scbdata returns 0.
note: Slice shows the later part; the head (6225-6283) was read only for the saved_stack allocation. Reviewer round 15 not supported: init_level++ comes after each successful stage (aic79xx.c:6300, 6327, 6337, 6371), so a failed stage does not increment it except that the increment at 6371 precedes ahd_init_scbdata. Callees not read.

name: ahd_action
prose: CAM SIM action entry point (aic79xx_osm.c:462-728, void; the slice is the middle of it). It finds the softc from the sim and dispatches on ccb->ccb_h.func_code. With AHD_TARGET_MODE: XPT_ACCEPT_TARGET_IO is queued on the LUN's accept_tios list (status CAM_REQ_INPROG, no xpt_done here) and the target queue FIFO is run if it was blocked; XPT_CONT_TARGET_IO is not queued but turned into an SCB: if the target device lookup fails it is routed to the black-hole LUN, and the common SCB-setup code below then runs (fall-through) with our_id and target_id swapped. XPT_SCSI_IO, XPT_RESET_DEV and the continued target I/O share the SCB path: when the initiator role is off it completes the ccb with an error (xpt_done, return); it fetches an SCB, and if none is available it sets the status to resource-unavailable, freezes the queue as needed, calls xpt_done and returns; otherwise it fills the SCB (reset-device message, tag/disconnect flags, target-mode status flags) and hands it on for DMA setup and execution (error from the mapping completes the ccb via xpt_done). XPT_EN_LUN is completed immediately through xpt_done. XPT_ABORT, XPT_SET_TRAN_SETTINGS, XPT_GET_TRAN_SETTINGS, XPT_CALC_GEOMETRY, XPT_RESET_BUS, XPT_TERM_IO and XPT_PATH_INQ fill in their results and complete with xpt_done; an unknown function code sets an error status and completes with xpt_done. So not all requests are completed by this function itself: the accepted target IO is queued, and SCSI I/O completes asynchronously after the SCB runs.
note: Real function is ahd_action. Reviewer round 15 right (XPT_EN_LUN is completed via xpt_done, and XPT_CONT_TARGET_IO is set up as an SCB, not queued, 482-518 and 632-635). Partly read: the SCB-setup body (lines 520-630) and the XPT_PATH_INQ and transfer-settings handling were skimmed for their completion calls only.

name: ahc_parse_msg
prose: Parses one incoming SCSI message for the AIC7xxx (aic7xxx.c:3058-3473, returns the loop state: MSGLOOP_IN_PROG, MSGLOOP_MSGCOMPLETE or MSGLOOP_TERMINATED; the slice is its middle). It starts with done = MSGLOOP_IN_PROG, response = FALSE, reject = FALSE and switches on msgin_buf[0]: DISCONNECT, SAVEDATAPOINTER, CMDCOMPLETE, RESTOREPOINTERS and IGN_WIDE_RESIDUE give MSGLOOP_TERMINATED (handled elsewhere); MESSAGE_REJECT calls ahc_handle_msg_reject and its result becomes response, then (falls through) NOOP gives MSGLOOP_MSGCOMPLETE; MSG_EXTENDED waits for enough bytes (index checks leave done as IN_PROG), then by the extended message type: SDTR (wrong length rejects) takes the period and offset, filters them with ahc_devlimited_syncrate and ahc_validate_offset and DOES apply them with ahc_set_syncrate (active and goal, aic7xxx.c:3150); if the SDTR was a reply to our own request an offset that changed rejects it, else it constructs an SDTR reply (response = TRUE); WDTR and PPR messages are handled similarly (validate, set width and sync rate, reject when the settings were widened relative to what was sent or the length is wrong, construct a reply when initiated by the target); an unknown extended message sets reject; BUS DEVICE RESET and the abort messages run ahc_handle_devreset or clean up the target-mode LUN state and give MSGLOOP_TERMINATED (the abort messages reject unless acting as a target); any other message sets reject. If reject is set it prepares a MESSAGE_REJECT reply (msgout), sets done = MSGLOOP_MSGCOMPLETE and response = TRUE. If done is not IN_PROG and there was no response it clears the message-in index; it returns done.
note: Real function is ahc_parse_msg; slice cut the head. Reviewer round 15 WRONG: ahc_set_syncrate is called in the SDTR path (aic7xxx.c:3150). Partly read: the WDTR and PPR extended-message bodies (3190-3400) were skimmed for their reject, response and set calls. Callees not read.

name: ahc_reset
prose: Resets the AIC7xxx chip (aic7xxx.c:4094-4194, returns int). It calls ahc_pause itself, so the caller does not need to have paused the chip. It saves SXFRCTL1 of channel A (and, on an AIC7770, channel B by selecting it through SBLKCTL), writes CHIPRST to HCNTRL and waits up to 1000 iterations of 1000 us for CHIPRSTACK (printing a warning if the reset did not finish but continuing anyway), then restores HCNTRL to the paused value. It determines the channel configuration from SBLKCTL (SELBUSB cleared for PCI chips): a single narrow channel needs nothing, wide sets AHC_WIDE, twin sets AHC_TWIN; any other combination prints 'Unsupported adapter type' and returns -1 immediately, BEFORE the saved SXFRCTL1 values are written back, so on that path SXFRCTL1 is not restored. Otherwise it writes back SXFRCTL1 (channel B first for twin channel chips, then channel A), and returns 0, or, if reinit is non-zero, the result of ahc->bus_chip_init(ahc).
note: Reviewers: original right (ahc_pause is called inside, 4106); round 15 right (the unsupported-configuration return at 4159-4160 skips the SXFRCTL1 restore). Callees not read.

name: ahc_handle_en_lun
prose: Handles an XPT_EN_LUN ccb (enable or disable target-mode LUN) (aic7xxx.c:7268-7634, void; the packet name ahc_enable_lun does not exist). It reports its result by setting ccb->ccb_h.status and does not call xpt_done itself. It first looks the target/LUN state up with ahc_find_tmode_devs (a failure becomes the ccb status and returns). It validates the requested target id against our id and the chip's multi-role/multi-tid features (CAM_TID_INVALID), and, if target role is not enabled yet, refuses with CAM_BUSY when commands are pending, or tries to switch the chip to target mode (a failure gives CAM_FUNC_NOTAVAIL). Enable path: CAM_LUN_ALRDY_ENA if the LUN already exists; CAM_REQ_INVALID for a non-zero group-6 CDB length; CAM_RESRC_UNAVAIL if the target state, the LUN state (malloc) or its CAM path cannot be allocated (the LUN state is freed when the path creation fails); otherwise it pauses the chip, registers the target id in the TARGID registers (or via SCSIID/SBLKCTL on chips without multi-tid), updates SCSISEQ for the black-hole LUN, unpauses and sets CAM_REQ_CMP. Disable path: CAM_LUN_INVALID if the LUN does not exist; it rejects with CAM_REQ_INVALID if a CONT_TARGET_IO ccb is still pending on that path, aborts all pending accept-TIO and immediate-notify ccbs (CAM_REQ_ABORTED, each completed with xpt_done), and if the status is still CAM_REQ_CMP it frees the LUN path and state, pauses the chip, frees an empty target state and its TARGID bit, restores SCSISEQ when no LUNs remain enabled, and unpauses. Paths that return early leave the chip state as it was at that point.
note: Real function is ahc_handle_en_lun. Partly read: lines 7295-7345 (target-id validation) and 7414-7450 (TARGID/SCSIID register programming) were only skimmed. Callees not read.

name: al_eth_change_mtu
prose: Static int (al_eth.c:3011-3025) applying a new MTU to the adapter. It performs no validation of new_mtu. It computes max_frame = new_mtu + ETHER_HDR_LEN + ETHER_CRC_LEN + ETHER_VLAN_ENCAP_LEN, calls al_eth_req_rx_buff_size(adapter, new_mtu) (which chooses the receive buffer size, not examined here, so what size adapter->rx_mbuf_sz ends up with is decided there), logs a debug message, calls al_eth_rx_pkt_limit_config with the frame range AL_ETH_MIN_FRAME_LEN..max_frame, and al_eth_tso_mss_config with an MSS of new_mtu - 100 (so a new_mtu below 100 gives a negative argument converted to the callee's parameter type). It returns 0 in every case; errors of the callees are not examined.
note: Reviewers: original right (the old formal precondition was weaker than the validation claimed in the prose; new_mtu - 100 is used, 3022); round 2 concerns al_eth_req_rx_buff_size internals (not read). Hardware callees not read.

name: al_eth_lm_link_detection
prose: Link-manager step that checks the link and detects a mode change (al_init_eth_lm.c:1147-1270, returns int: 0 or the error of module detection). lm_context, old_mode and new_mode must be non-NULL (al_assert); link_fault may be NULL. If lm_pause is configured and returns true it sets *new_mode = DISCONNECTED, sets *link_fault (when given) to false if the link state is UP, else true, and returns 0 at once; on this path *old_mode is NOT written and lm_context->link_state is not updated from hardware. Otherwise it sets *old_mode and *new_mode to the current mode and *link_fault to true, then by link_state: UP reads the hardware status; if the link is up it clears *link_fault, sets the LED on and returns 0; otherwise it moves the state to DOWN (local fault) or DOWN_RF and continues; DOWN_RF reads the status: a local fault moves to DOWN and continues, else, with no remote fault, it moves the state to UP, and in this branch (whether or not it moved to UP) it returns 0 immediately, leaving *link_fault true and *new_mode equal to the current mode (not a newly detected one); DOWN continues. After that it turns the LED off and detects the module: with sfp_detection it calls al_eth_module_detect (an error is logged and returned) and stores the result in lm_context->mode and *new_mode, else it uses default_mode. If the mode changed it logs it, marks rx/tx parameters dirty, sets new_port and, if a LED configuration callback exists and the new mode is not DISCONNECTED, calls it with the speed for the mode (an unknown mode logs an error but the callback is still called). Returns 0.
note: Reviewers: original right (the lm_pause early return leaves *old_mode unset and does not update link_state); round 15 right (the DOWN_RF to UP path returns with *link_fault true and new_mode unchanged, 1204-1217). Callees not read.

name: ale_dma_alloc
prose: Allocates the DMA tags, rings and maps of the Atheros AR81xx driver (if_ale.c:999-1281, returns int; the slice is the middle of it). It computes the page size from the guard size (jumbo or normal frame length) and starts with lowaddr = BUS_SPACE_MAXADDR. It creates parent and per-ring tags (Tx ring, Rx pages, Tx CMB, Rx CMBs), allocates and loads the ring, page and CMB memory, and, for each load, treats 'error != 0 || ctx.ale_busaddr == 0' as a failure: it prints a message and jumps to fail. Because fail only returns the current value of error, a load whose callback left ale_busaddr at 0 while the bus_dmamap_load error was 0 returns 0 (success) even though the allocation failed. After the ring allocations, if lowaddr is not already 32-bit it calls ale_check_boundary: if the 4 GB boundary was crossed it prints a message, frees everything with ale_dma_free, sets lowaddr to 32-bit and restarts from the 'again' label (once). It then creates the Tx buffer parent tag and Tx tag and a DMA map for each Tx ring entry (a failure prints a message and goes to fail). Nothing is freed on the fail path here (the caller cleans up); the function returns error, which is 0 on full success or the last bus_dma error (or 0 in the busaddr == 0 case above).
note: Slice cut the head. Reviewer round 15 right (the 'return 0 when bus_dmamap_load leaves a zero bus address' case, if_ale.c lines near 1127-1130 and 1280). Partly read: the individual tag-creation argument lists were not read. Callees not read.

name: ale_watchdog
prose: Static void (if_ale.c:1898-1921) run from the periodic tick, with the driver lock asserted. It returns without doing anything if the watchdog timer is 0 or, after being decremented, is still non-zero. When the timer reaches 0 it checks the link flag: if there is no link it prints 'watchdog timeout (lost link)' first, then increments the OERRORS counter, clears IFF_DRV_RUNNING, calls ale_init_locked and returns without restarting the send queue. With a link it prints 'watchdog timeout -- resetting', increments OERRORS, clears IFF_DRV_RUNNING, calls ale_init_locked, and, if the interface send queue is not empty, calls ale_start_locked to restart transmission.
note: Reviewers: original right (the lost-link branch resets and returns without restarting a non-empty send queue, 1908-1914); round 15 right (the message is printed before OERRORS is incremented and before the reset, 1909-1912).

name: ata_interrupt_locked
prose: Interrupt handler body for an ATA channel (ata-all.c:356-388, void). If the channel has a hw.status callback and it reports no interrupt for this device (returns false) the function returns at once. It returns if there is no running request. If the channel state is ATA_IDLE it prints 'interrupt on idle channel ignored' with device_printf (a diagnostic is emitted) and returns without further effect. Otherwise it calls ch->hw.end_transaction(request); only when that returns ATA_OP_FINISHED it clears ch->running, sets the state to ATA_IDLE only if it was ATA_ACTIVE (other states are left unchanged), and calls ata_cam_end_transaction(ch->dev, request); any other return value of end_transaction leaves the request running and changes nothing here.
note: Reviewers: original right (the state becomes ATA_IDLE only if it was ATA_ACTIVE, 383-384); round 15 right (the idle-channel branch prints a diagnostic before returning, 372-375).

name: ata_begin_transaction
prose: Starts an ATA/ATAPI transaction (ata-lowlevel.c:82-237, returns ATA_OP_FINISHED or ATA_OP_CONTINUES, not an errno; errors are stored in request->result). It first clears ATA_R_DMA from the request flags for channels that cannot do ATAPI DMA (or ATAPI DMA reads only). By (ATAPI, DMA) flags: PIO (default): issues the command with ch->hw.command (on failure prints a message, result = EIO, finish); an ATA_DEVICE_RESET command is a finished path that polls status for up to about 10 s, reads the error register if the error bit is set, reads the task file and finishes with request->result left unchanged (0), i.e. a success result with ATA_OP_FINISHED; for a PIO write it waits for READY|DRQ (timeout: message, EIO, finish) and writes the first data block; then it continues. DMA: loads the DMA map (error: message, result = error, finish), starts DMA before or after the command depending on ATA_DMA_BEFORE_CMD, with EIO and finish on a command or DMA-start error; then continues. ATAPI PIO and ATAPI DMA: a POLL_DSC request selects the drive, waits 10 us and sets result = EBUSY if DSC is not set, then finishes (the request status and error fields are not updated on this path); otherwise it issues the packet command (and for DMA loads and starts DMA), with EIO or the load error on failures; then continues. A value falling outside the switch prints 'ata_begin_transaction OOPS!!!' and falls into the finish label. On every finish path it unloads the DMA map if there is an unload method and returns ATA_OP_FINISHED; on the continue path it arms the request callout (timeout * hz, ata_timeout) and returns ATA_OP_CONTINUES.
note: Reviewers: original right (the successful ATA_OP_FINISHED paths, device reset and POLL_DSC, leave result at 0, which is not an errno failure); round 15 right (the POLL_DSC path does not set request->status or error, 176-182 and 195-201). Callees not read.

name: ata_nvidia_status
prose: Static int (ata-nvidia.c:281-307) reading and acknowledging the NVIDIA SATA interrupt status for one channel. The register offset is 0x0440 when the chip config has the NV4 flag and 0x0010 otherwise (NV4, not NVQ, selects the offset); the per-channel bit shift is ch->unit shifted left by 4 when the NVQ flag is set (NVQ selects the register width, 32-bit versus 8-bit and the shift width) and by 2 otherwise. It reads the status with a 32-bit read for NVQ chips or an 8-bit read otherwise, calls ata_sata_phy_check_events(dev, -1) if any of the 0x0c bits for this channel (the shifted mask) are set, writes back the acknowledge value (0x0f << shift, with 0x00f000f0 ORed in for the 32-bit case; the write clears the channel's bits) and returns istatus & (0x01 << shift), the raw masked bit value, which is 0 or (1 << shift), not necessarily 1.
note: Reviewers: original right (the return value is the masked bit, not 0 or 1); round 15 right (NV4 selects the offset and NVQ the access width and shift, 285-286). The device-specific register layout was not checked beyond the code.

name: ar5212AniLowerImmunity
prose: Static void (ar5212_ani.c:809-881) that lowers one ANI immunity setting by one step, performing at most one adjustment per call (each branch returns after one ar5212AniControl call). It asserts ANI is enabled. If RSSI-based ANI is enabled (ANI_ENA_RSSI) it reads the beacon RSSI and: for RSSI above the high threshold it takes no action in this block (falls to the spur and noise steps below); for RSSI above the low threshold it first re-enables OFDM weak-signal detection (ar5212AniControl(HAL_ANI_OFDM_WEAK_SIGNAL_DETECTION, AH_TRUE), i.e. it can ENABLE detection, not lower it) if it is currently off and returns, else lowers the first-step level by one if it is above 0 and returns; for RSSI at or below the low threshold it lowers the first-step level if above 0 and returns. If RSSI-based ANI is disabled, that whole block is skipped (the first-step level is not touched by it). Then, if nothing returned: it lowers the spur immunity level by one if above 0 (return), else lowers the noise immunity level by one if above 0. If every level is already 0 it does nothing.
note: Reviewers: original right (the weak-signal branch enables detection with AH_TRUE rather than lowering anything, 832-838); round 15 right (the first-step lowering is inside the ANI_ENA_RSSI block, so it is skipped when RSSI ANI is disabled, 819-861).

name: ar5212SetCapability
prose: Sets a hardware capability on an AR5212 (ar5212_misc.c:930-1047, returns HAL_BOOL AH_TRUE/AH_FALSE). By type: TKIP_MIC sets or clears the MIC-enable bit in the saved STA_ID1 defaults and returns AH_TRUE; TKIP_SPLIT returns AH_FALSE if the chip lacks TX/RX MIC key support, else updates ah_miscMode, ORs it into AR_MISC_MODE and returns AH_TRUE; DIVERSITY switches on `capability`: 0 returns AH_FALSE; 1 (setting) updates the CCK-detect antenna fast-diversity bit only when the PHY is powered and capability equals HAL_CAP_STRONG_DIV, stores ah_diversity, and returns AH_TRUE regardless of whether the PHY is powered; HAL_CAP_STRONG_DIV returns AH_FALSE when the PHY is off, else writes the diversity gain control field and returns AH_TRUE; any other value returns AH_FALSE. DIAG writes AR_DIAG_SW; TPC sets ah_tpcEnabled; MCAST_KEYSRCH sets or clears a STA_ID1 bit; TPC_ACK and TPC_CTS add the TX power index offset, cap the value at 63, update the TPC register fields and write AR_TPC (all return AH_TRUE); INTMIT maps `capability` (0..6) to an ANI command and returns the result of ah_aniControl (which may be AH_FALSE), or AH_FALSE for an out-of-range capability; TSF_ADJUST sets or clears the TX_ADD_TSF bit and returns AH_TRUE only if the chip supports it, otherwise it falls through into the default case (there is no break or return), which calls ath_hal_setcapability(ah, type, capability, setting, status) and returns its result; the default case does the same.
note: Reviewers: original right (diversity capability 1 returns AH_TRUE even when the PHY is off, 960-972); round 15 right (the HAL_CAP_INTMIT path returns the ah_aniControl result, 1017-1031). Callees not read.

name: ar5212GetNf
prose: Reads, filters and re-loads the noise floor for a channel (ar5212_reset.c:1390-1474, returns int16_t). If the AGC NF-calibration bit is still set (calibration not complete) it stores h->privNF (the most recent value) into ichan->rawNoiseFloor, returns it and changes no register. Otherwise it reads the noise floor nf; if a threshold exists and nf > threshold it marks the channel CWINT and sets nf = 0, and if no threshold is available it also sets nf = 0. It adds nf to the history buffer. During the warm-up phase (h->first_run): an nf below AR5212_CCA_MIN_BAD_VALUE or above AR5212_CCA_MAX_HIGH_VALUE (including the nf = 0 set above) is replaced by AR5212_CCA_MAX_GOOD_VALUE and the invalid counter is reset; otherwise the counter is decremented and, when it reaches 0, first_run is cleared and nf and privNF become the median of the history buffer; before that nf is AR5212_CCA_MAX_GOOD_VALUE. After warm-up (first_run clear) nf and privNF are always set to the median of the history buffer, so an out-of-range reading no longer produces AR5212_CCA_MAX_GOOD_VALUE but the median. It then loads nf into AR_PHY(25), toggles the AGC NF control bits to start a calibration, waits for it to complete (a timeout only prints a debug message), loads a fixed -50 dBm into the register, re-enables NF updates and starts another calibration, and returns ichan->rawNoiseFloor = nf.
note: Reviewers: original right (a threshold violation nf = 0 is overwritten by the warm-up or median logic and the in-progress path returns privNF); round 15 right (after warm-up an out-of-range nf returns the median, not AR5212_CCA_MAX_GOOD_VALUE, 1443-1445). Callees not read.

name: ar5416ProcessRadarEvent
prose: Converts a radar PHY-error frame into a DFS event (ar5416_radar.c:233-420, returns HAL_BOOL; the packet name dfs_process_phy_err does not exist). It returns AH_FALSE unless rs_phyerr is HAL_PHYERR_RADAR or HAL_PHYERR_FALSE_RADAR_EXT. It reads the capability flags (ext channel, enhanced DFS, combined RSSI), selects rssi (combined or control chain 0) and ext_rssi, and zeroes either one if its top bit (0x80) is set. With ext-channel DFS support it needs at least 3 bytes of data (AH_FALSE if datalen < 3) and reads the primary pulse length, extension pulse length and bandwidth info from the last three bytes of buf (buf is indexed by datalen); it returns AH_FALSE if pulse_bw_info is 0. Without ext-channel support it takes the duration from buf[0] (0 if there is no data) and returns AH_FALSE when both the duration and rssi are 0. With ext-channel support it picks the pulse: radar found on both channels sets is_dc and uses the longer pulse; early-extension, primary-only or extension-only cases select the corresponding duration and flags. With enhanced DFS it adjusts rssi by the pulse_bw_info case (zeroing it or taking ext_rssi, using 3 dB and 12 dB margins); with ext-channel support but not enhanced DFS it uses ext_rssi if larger (and below 128). It fills event->re_full_ts, re_ts, re_rssi, re_dur and re_flags (PRICH, EXTCH, EXTEARLY, ISDC as applicable) and returns AH_TRUE.
note: Real function is ar5416ProcessRadarEvent; the slice cut the head. Reading of buf and the exact bandwidth bit macros (EXT_CH_RADAR_FOUND etc.) were taken from the code as is.

name: ar5416ResetTxQueue
prose: Programs the hardware registers of one TX queue (ar5416_xmit.c:1243-1497, returns HAL_BOOL; the slice cut the head and the function is not unnamed). It returns AH_FALSE (with a debug message) if q is not below the chip's total queue count, and returns AH_TRUE without touching any register if the queue is HAL_TX_QUEUE_INACTIVE. Otherwise it computes cwMin (the default contention window from the channel type, rounded up to 2^n - 1, when tqi_cwmin is HAL_TXQ_USEDEFAULT, else the configured value) and writes the DCU local IFS (cwmin, cwmax, aifs), the retry limits (initial short/long station retries and the queue's long/short frame retry values), and the other DCU/QCU control registers (misc, backoff threshold, ready time, scheduling flags); then, by queue type, applies type-specific settings: beacon queues get beacon-specific QCU/DCU flags and timers, CAB queues set the ready-time handling (defaulting a ready time when the driver supplied none), PS-poll and UAPSD queues set their QCU flags, and other types add nothing. It enables the queue's interrupt bits as needed and returns AH_TRUE.
note: Real function is ar5416ResetTxQueue. Partly read: the register-by-register setup in lines 1300-1490 (the DCU/QCU bit fields and the per-type flags) was only skimmed for its structure and returns; no claim is made about which bits are set.

name: ar9280Attach
prose: Attaches an AR9280 (Merlin) chip (ar9280_attach.c:149-423, returns struct ath_hal * or AH_NULL; the slice cut the head). It allocates the HAL state (on failure sets *status = HAL_ENOMEM and returns AH_NULL), installs the 9280-specific method pointers and calibration tables, resets the chip (ar5416SetResetReg) and wakes it (ar5416SetPowerMode), and selects the INI register tables for Merlin 2.0 or later versus earlier revisions. It then runs the chip reset and self-test, reads the PHY revision, and checks the analog 5 GHz revision (unsupported chips give HAL_ENOTSUPP); it sets up the RF (ar9280RfAttach), reads the EEPROM power-table and clock settings, and, for Merlin 2.0, selects the RX gain INI table and the TX gain INI table from the EEPROM gain type. For an unknown RX or TX gain type the code does HALASSERT(AH_FALSE) and then jumps to the bad label (so in a build without assertions the attach fails with ecode as it stood, instead of continuing; the comment says 'try to continue' but the code does not). It then fills the capability information (failure: HAL_EEREAD), checks the final ecode, sets the misc mode, ANI and noise-floor limits for 2 GHz and 5 GHz, and returns ah. Every failure path goes to bad, which calls ah->ah_detach(ah) if ah is set, stores ecode in *status if status is non-NULL and returns AH_NULL. The status pointer is dereferenced only on failure paths after the allocation (a NULL status is tolerated at bad).
note: Real function is ar9280Attach. Reviewer round 15 right (an unknown RX/TX gain type ends in goto bad, 345-350 and 364-369). Partly read: the INI table setup and the EEPROM-dependent options (lines 275-330) were only skimmed. Callees not read.

name: _ath_power_setpower
prose: Void function (if_ath.c:299-342) that records a target power state and applies it if allowed. It asserts the ATH lock, logs a debug line, and always stores power_state in sc->sc_target_powerstate. It then acts only if (the power-save reference count is 0 or the requested state is HAL_PM_AWAKE) and the requested state differs from sc_cur_powerstate: it stores the new current state and calls ath_hal_setpower(sc->sc_ah, power_state) (this call happens whenever that outer condition holds, whether or not selfgen is non-zero); and if selfgen is non-zero, the current state is now awake, and sc_target_selfgen_state is not awake, it also calls ath_hal_setselfgenpower with the target selfgen state. If the outer condition is false (reference count held and a sleep request, or no change of state) only the target state was updated and the hardware is left alone. file and line are used only for the log message.
note: Reviewers: original right (the selfgen argument and the target_selfgen_state != HAL_PM_AWAKE condition were missing, 335-337); round 15 right (ath_hal_setpower is called whenever the outer condition holds, independent of selfgen, 322-325).

name: ath_newstate
prose: net80211 state-change method of the ath driver (if_ath.c:5815-6256, returns int; the slice is the early to middle part). It sets the LED for the new state, requests awake power (ath_power_setselfgen unless going to SLEEP, and the power state), and, for the SCAN state, restores awake power and enables the global interrupts before continuing. It computes the RX filter and a 'stamode' flag (STA, AHDEMO or IBSS); only when stamode is true AND the new state is RUN does it set sc_curaid and sc_curbssid from the node and call ath_hal_setassocid; so the association id and bssid are updated in those modes only, not on every successful change. It installs the RX filter and, for non-STA modes, updates the MAC address of valid key cache entries. It then calls the vap's saved av_newstate (an error goes to bad, restoring power state and returning the error). For the RUN state, by opmode: HOSTAP, IBSS, MBSS and AHDEMO (the latter only with TDMA capability) stop beacon DMA, allocate the beacon (ath_beacon_alloc, error goes to bad) and then, for an IBSS node with a current TSF, defer beacon timer setup (sc_syncbeacon = 1), else if beacons are not yet configured call ath_tdma_config (TDMA) or ath_beacon_config and set sc_beacons; the STA mode defers beacon configuration to the next beacon (so STA does not allocate a beacon here); other modes do nothing. It then updates noise-floor processing, power, and the calibration callout. INIT, SLEEP and SCAN states stop timers, interrupts or calibrations as appropriate. At the end it restores the power state with ath_power_restore_power_state and returns error.
note: Reviewers: original right (associd/bssid and beacon state are only updated for specific modes and states); round 15 right (beacon setup applies to HOSTAP/IBSS/MBSS and TDMA AHDEMO, associd/bssid to STA/AHDEMO/IBSS in RUN, 5912-5915 and 6003-6052). Partly read: lines 5930-5992, 6060-6256 were only scanned for state-specific calls and returns.

name: ath_node_set_tim
prose: Sets or clears the TIM bit for a node (if_ath.c:6778-6887, returns int: whether the TIM changed). It has two builds. Without ATH_SW_PSQ it returns 0 if the vap's av_set_tim hook is NULL and otherwise returns av_set_tim(ni, enable) (the NULL check is present here too). With ATH_SW_PSQ it takes ATH_TX_LOCK itself (it must not be called with that lock held), stores an_stack_psq = enable, and if av_set_tim is NULL unlocks and returns 0. Then: if enable is set and an_tim_set is already 1 it only logs, unlocks and returns 0 (the request is ignored, an_tim_set stays 1); if enable is set otherwise it sets an_tim_set = 1, unlocks and returns av_set_tim(ni, enable); if enable is clear and the software queue depth is 0 it clears an_tim_set, unlocks and returns av_set_tim(ni, 0); if enable is clear, the queue is not empty and the node is no longer in power save it also clears an_tim_set and calls av_set_tim; otherwise (clear requested, packets queued, node asleep) it unlocks, logs and returns 0 without changing the TIM. The av_set_tim call is made after the lock is dropped.
note: Reviewers: original right (the call is ignored when an_tim_set is already 1 and the function takes ATH_TX_LOCK itself, 6787 and 6816-6823); round 15 WRONG: the non-ATH_SW_PSQ build does check av_set_tim for NULL (if_ath.c:6882-6883).

name: ath_lna_rx_comb_scan
prose: Void function (if_ath_lna_div.c:704-1010; the packet name ath_ant_div_comb_scan does not exist, the slice is the later half of ath_lna_rx_comb_scan) called for received frames to drive the LNA/antenna diversity combining scan. It decodes the main and alternate RSSI and antenna configuration from the rx status and returns at once if LNA diversity is not enabled (sc_dolnadiv) or the TX antenna is not HAL_ANT_VARIABLE. It accumulates packet and RSSI totals per antenna when both RSSI values are positive. It decides short_scan (when scanning with a good alternate: the short-scan interval elapsed, or the short-scan packet count was reached with a low alternate ratio) and returns without changes if fewer than the maximum number of packets has been collected (or the frame is part of an aggregate) and no short scan is due. Otherwise it computes the alternate-antenna ratio and the average RSSI per antenna, reads the current diversity configuration from the HAL (ath_hal_div_comb_conf_get), increments the scan counter and, when it reaches the maximum, evaluates whether the alternate antenna is good (ath_lnaconf_alt_good_scan) and starts the scan (scan = true, scan_not_start = true). Outside a scan it switches the main and alternate LNA configurations when the alternate ratio is high or by the current main set, and goes to div_comb_done in those cases; during a scan it steps through the LNA1/LNA2/ADD/SUB configurations by the current alternate set and the measured RSSI values, and finally adjusts the fast diversity bias (ath_ant_adjust_fast_divbias). At div_comb_done it writes the new configuration back to the HAL when changed, logs the changes, resets scan_start_time to ticks and zeroes the packet and RSSI counters.
note: Real function is ath_lna_rx_comb_scan; the slice cut the head. Partly read: the scan-state switch bodies (lines 910-960, 1030-1060 region) and the helper calls were only skimmed; the exact LNA configuration chosen in each case is not claimed. Helpers not read.

name: proc_synaptics
prose: Processes one Synaptics TouchPad absolute-mode packet (psm.c:3264-3677, returns int; the packet name psm_process_synaptics_packet does not exist, the slice is the middle of proc_synaptics). It returns 0 immediately if synaptics support is disabled, and -1 (discard) if the packet's framing bits are wrong (ipacket[0] & 0xc8 != 0x80 or ipacket[3] & 0xc8 != 0xc0). It starts from ms->button = ms->obutton, decodes the finger count (W value, extended-W codes for multi-finger and fuzzy-finger reports, keeping some state in static variables) and the button bits (physical, extended/guest buttons, clickpad). For the extended-W packets it records the extra finger info and jumps to SYNAPTICS_END (skipping position processing). If sc->syninfo.touchpad_off is set it also jumps to SYNAPTICS_END (psm.c:3453-3454), skipping the finger tracking, palm detection and gestures. Otherwise it runs psmpalmdetect on the first finger; when no palm is detected it runs gesture detection, then smooths every finger's position into x and y. If a palm was detected it sets *x = *y = *z = 0, restores ms->button = ms->obutton and returns 0 immediately (this palm early return is separate from the touchpad_off path). Otherwise it ORs the extended and guest buttons into ms->button. At SYNAPTICS_END it turns the extra buttons 4-7 into a scroll-wheel value in *z (-1, 1, -2, 2, else 0), clears those button bits from ms->button and returns 0.
note: Real function is proc_synaptics; slice cut the head. Reviewer round 17 right that the touchpad_off case is a separate path from palm detection (goto SYNAPTICS_END at 3454 versus the palm return at 3643). Partly read: the finger decoding and EVDEV-specific code (3345-3640) was skimmed.

name: proc_elantech
prose: Processes one Elantech touchpad packet (psm.c:4389-4842, returns int: 0 processed or ignored, -1 for an out-of-sync/invalid packet; the packet name elantech_get_packet does not exist, this slice is the early part of proc_elantech). It returns 0 at once if elantech support is disabled. It classifies the packet: a debounce packet is NOP; a track-point packet (when the hardware has one) is TRACKPOINT; otherwise by hardware version: v2 returns -1 unless the packet looks like v2 (then 2-finger or common), v3 returns -1 unless it is a v3 head or tail packet (then V3), v4 distinguishes status/head/motion packets by byte 3 and returns -1 for an unknown code, and an unknown hardware version returns -1. Then the per-format decoding: V2 common/2-finger read the finger positions and buttons; V3 head and tail packets assemble multi-finger positions across two packets and return 0 early when more data is needed; V4 status packets track the finger-count bitmask and return 0 early for a repeated status; V4 head packets fill one finger's position (returning 0 early under some conditions) and V4 motion packets update positions of several fingers.
note: Slice cut the head; the same function is described by the next item. Partly read: the per-version bit decoding (4439-4650) was skimmed for returns and packet classification, not read line by line.

name: proc_elantech
prose: Later part of proc_elantech (psm.c:4389-4842, returns int). After the per-format decoding of the packet types (V4 head, V4 motion, track-point, NOP), the track-point packet reports its relative movement and buttons and returns 0 early; a NOP packet returns 0 and an unknown packet type returns -1 (the default case, which is reached only after the earlier classification code has accepted the packet, so it is a defensive return). The remaining code, for touchpad packets, applies palm detection (psmpalmdetect) and, if no palm is found, gesture handling (psmgestures), smooths the finger positions into *x, *y, converts the buttons (including the clickpad button and the left/right/middle bits), and, when a palm was detected, zeroes the motion and returns 0 (psm.c:4824); otherwise it sets *z and the button state in ms and returns 0 at the end (4841).
note: Reviewers: round 15 right that the default -1 path occurs after packet classification has already filtered (default at 4752-4753). Partly read: lines 4750-4842 (smoothing, buttons) were skimmed.

name: BHNDB_IO_MISC(_type, _ptr, _op, _size)
prose: Macro (bhndb.c:1823-1833) that generates one static void bus method 'bhndb_bus_<op>_<size>(device_t dev, device_t child, struct bhnd_resource *r, bus_size_t offset, _type _ptr datap, bus_size_t count)'; BHNDB_IO_METHODS instantiates it for read_multi, write_multi, their _stream variants, set_multi, set_region, read_region, write_region and their _stream variants, for 1, 2 and 4 byte types (BHNDB_IO_METHODS(uint8_t, 1), (uint16_t, 2), (uint32_t, 4)). Each generated function does the common setup (BHNDB_IO_COMMON_SETUP(sizeof(_type) * count)): it takes the softc, locks the bhndb softc lock (BHNDB_LOCK), asks bhndb_io_resource for a dynamic window resource covering offset .. offset + sizeof(type) * count of the child's resource (possibly 'stealing' a window, recording the restore address), takes the parent resource, and KASSERTs that the child resource is not a direct resource and that the window resource is active (these checks only exist when KASSERT is compiled in). It then performs the corresponding bus_<op>_<size> on the window resource at the translated offset, and the common teardown: if a window was stolen it returns it (bhndb_dw_return_stolen with the saved restore address) and always unlocks. The generated functions return nothing; they have no error path of their own, and a failure to obtain a window is handled inside bhndb_io_resource (not read).
note: Macro-generated; the name is the definition head of the generator macro (the generated names are bhndb_bus_read_multi_1 ... bhndb_bus_write_region_stream_4). Reviewers: none beyond the mechanical round. Callees bhndb_io_resource and bhndb_dw_return_stolen not read.

name: bhndb_attach
prose: Generic bhndb(4) attach helper (bhndb.c:509-607, returns int; the packet name bhndb_generic_attach does not exist, and the slice also shows the following detach/suspend/resume functions). It copies dev, the parent device, the bridge core and chip id into the softc and initialises the service registry (its error is returned immediately, with nothing else set up). It initialises the softc lock, looks up a hardware spec for the core list (if none is found it prints a message and uses the parent's generic hwcfg), allocates the bridge resources (NULL gives ENOMEM, via failed), adds the 'bhnd' child bus device (NULL gives ENXIO), marks its dinfo as bridged, allocates an EROM parser over a new iores (failure: finalises the I/O object and ENXIO), obtains the hardware priority table and initialises the region configuration (an error is printed and returned). On success it frees the EROM, sets it to NULL and returns 0. The failed label destroys the softc lock, frees the bridge resources if allocated, frees the EROM if allocated, finalises the service registry and returns the error. Note that the child bus device added with BUS_ADD_CHILD is not deleted on the failure paths.
note: Real function is bhndb_attach. Not reviewed beyond the mechanical rounds; checked against the code. Callees not read.

name: bhnd_pmu_spuravoid_pllupdate
prose: Static int (bhnd_pmu_subr.c:2976-3316) that reprograms the PMU PLL for spur avoidance mode `spuravoid` and returns 0 or ENODEV. It treats a BCM6362 revision 0 as a BCM43224. Per chip group it programs PLL control registers through BHND_PMU_PLL_WRITE: for BCM6362 (asserting rev != 0), BCM5357, BCM4749, BCM43235..43238, BCM43234, BCM43237 and BCM53572 it selects p1div/ndiv for NONE, M1 or M2 and writes PLLCTL0 and PLLCTL2 (offset +6 for BCM5357); BCM4331 writes PLLCTL0 and PLLCTL2 constants for NONE, M1 and M2; the BCM43224/43225/43226/43421 group writes PLLCTL0-5 for NONE and M1 only; BCM43111/43112/43222/43420, BCM4716/4748/47162, BCM4322/43221/43231/4342, BCM4336 and BCM43131/43227/43228/43428 each have their own constant sets (some modes unsupported); the BCM4319 case performs no PLL register writes at all and leaves pmuctrl 0. A mode that a chip group does not support returns ENODEV immediately, after possibly having written nothing, and an unknown chip logs 'unknown spuravoidance settings' and returns ENODEV without changing the PLL. After the switch it ORs the update bits (PLLCTL_UPD, or NOILP_ON_WAIT and others for the 4716 group) into BHND_PMU_CTRL if pmuctrl is non-zero (so BCM4319 does not update that control register) and returns 0.
note: Slice cut the head. Reviewer round 15 right (the BCM4319 case writes no PLL registers, so the old 'after programming the PLL control registers' claim is false). Partly read: the constant tables of each chip group (lines 3040-3290) were skimmed for their return paths and which registers are written.

name: bhnd_nvram_ident_num_string
prose: Static bool (bhnd_nvram_value_fmts.c:968-1050) that checks whether the ilen bytes at inp are a valid integer string and reports the base. It returns false for an empty string, for a string that ends right after an optional leading '-' or '+', and for a string that ends right after a '0x'/'0X' prefix. The prefix is recognised and skipped only when base is 16 or 0 (setting base to 16); when base is 0 and no hex prefix was seen, a leading '0' selects base 8 and any other start selects base 10. It then checks every remaining byte: it must be a decimal or hexadecimal digit (any other character returns false) whose value is below base (otherwise false), counting digits; it returns false if no digit was counted. On success, if obase is non-NULL it stores the (possibly detected) base in *obase and returns true; *obase is not written on a false return. No leading whitespace is skipped and no overflow check is made; the code does not validate the base argument itself, so a base other than 0, 8, 10 or 16 is accepted as long as every digit is below it (a base of 0 is the only value that triggers detection).
note: Name found: the item was named 'unnamed integer string parser'. Reviewer round 15's reason was truncated; checked against the code only.

name: bhnd_nvram_val_vprintf
prose: Formats an NVRAM value with a printf-style format (bhnd_nvram_value_prf.c:209-879, returns int; the slice is its tail, with the 's' and 'c' conversions and the epilogue). It takes the output limit from *olen when outp is non-NULL (else 0), walks the format string and the value's elements and produces output with the WRITE_CHAR macro, which stores a byte only while limit > nbytes but always counts it. The 's' conversion first asks bhnd_nvram_val_encode_elem for the string length (error returned), drops the trailing NUL from the length, writes right-adjust padding, encodes the string directly into the output buffer when space remains (an ENOMEM result is tolerated, any other error is returned), adds the length to nbytes (returning EFTYPE on size_t overflow) and writes left-adjust padding. The 'c' conversion encodes the element into a local char c (error returned) and asserts the encoded size is 1, writes right-adjust padding, but then calls WRITE_CHAR(padc), i.e. it writes the pad character instead of the encoded character c (the encoded value is never output), then the left-adjust padding. At the end it appends a terminating NUL if limit > nbytes, increments nbytes (EFTYPE if it would overflow), stores the required size nbytes in *olen, and returns ENOMEM if the limit is smaller than the required size and outp is non-NULL, else 0 (a NULL outp with a size query returns 0).
note: Real function is bhnd_nvram_val_vprintf; slice shows its tail. Reviewer round 17 right: the 'c' case writes padc instead of c (bhnd_nvram_value_prf.c:826-850, WRITE_CHAR(padc) at about 848). Not read: the format-parsing head (lines 225-760).

name: bnxt_queue_remap
prose: Static int (bnxt_dcb.c:198-241) that remaps traffic classes to hardware queues so lossless classes land on lossless queues; it returns 0 or the error of an HWRM configuration call. First loop: for each traffic class i < max_tc whose bit is set in lltc_mask it scans the receive queue info with index j for a queue whose profile is lossless (BNXT_LLQ), assigns tc_to_qidx[i] = j and marks j used in qmap; the scan over j has no upper bound check against the number of queues (it relies on enough lossless queues existing, so with too few lossless queues j can run past the array and the loop may not terminate within max_tc queues), and a lossless queue index above max_tc - 1 is recorded in tc_to_qidx but cannot be marked in a bitmap of only max bits meaningfully for the second pass. Second loop: for each class not in lltc_mask it takes the next zero bit of qmap in 0..max-1 (find_next_zero_bit(&qmap, max, j)) and assigns it, so tc_to_qidx is a permutation of 0..max_tc-1 only if every lossless class found a lossless queue with index below max_tc; otherwise it is not guaranteed to be a permutation. Then, if softc->ieee_ets is set, it configures the CoS bandwidth (bnxt_hwrm_queue_cos2bw_cfg) and the priority-to-CoS map (bnxt_hwrm_queue_pri2cos_cfg); the first non-zero result is printed and returned (tc_to_qidx has already been changed by then). It returns 0 otherwise.
note: Reviewers: original right (enough lossless queue profiles are required; tc_to_qidx is not guaranteed to be a permutation); round 15 right (lossless queues may lie beyond max_tc). Callees not read.

name: bnxt_qplib_post_send
prose: Posts one send work request to a QP's send queue (qplib_fp.c:1941-2291, returns int; the slice is the early to middle part). It returns -EINVAL (via done) if the QP state is neither RTS nor ERR, and -ENOMEM if the SQ does not have room for the needed slots plus the full-queue delta (messages are logged). Otherwise it takes the next software WQE entry, records the wr_id, type, flags, slot count and start PSN, and sets the signal-completion flag when the QP is signalled-by-default or the WQE asks for it. If the QP's current state is ERR (cur_qp_state) it does not write any WQE headers or data: it sets sch_handler and jumps to queue_err, which still advances the software queue entry, the hardware producer index and wqe_cnt, and the function returns 0 (the WQE is queued so that poll_cq can complete it in error). For a normal QP it zeroes the base and extension headers of the WQE, then puts the data: inline data (bnxt_qplib_put_inline) or the SGE list; a negative data_len (for example inline data that does not fit) jumps to queue_err WITHOUT setting rc, so the headers have already been zeroed and the work request is still counted and queued and the function returns 0 on that path. It then fills the headers by wqe->type (send, RDMA write/read, atomic, local invalidate, bind MW); an unknown type returns -EINVAL via done without advancing the queue. The PSN search/MSN entry is filled when needed, and queue_err/the tail advances the swq and producer index and increments wqe_cnt. At done, if sch_handler is set, it allocates nq_work (GFP_ATOMIC) and queues bnxt_qpn_cqn_sched_task on the CQ's workqueue; an allocation failure logs and sets rc = -ENOMEM (overriding 0). It returns rc.
note: Slice cut the head. Reviewers: original right (the ERR-QP path skips header and data fill and returns 0, 2002-2007 and 2015); round 15 right (on an inline overflow the headers are zeroed before bnxt_qplib_put_inline fails, 2013-2024). Partly read: the per-type WQE header filling (lines 2030-2230) was skimmed.

name: bnxt_qplib_cq_process_req
prose: Static int (qplib_fp.c:2911-3033) that turns one requester CQE into software CQEs for the send queue. It returns -EINVAL if the CQE's QP handle is NULL. It returns 0 without producing anything or advancing the queue if the SQ is already flushed, or if, for an error CQE on a variable-size WQE, the reported SQ consumer slot cannot be found (the lookup failure goes to done with rc still 0). Otherwise it walks the software WQE list from swq_last up to the consumer index reported by the CQE while the CQE budget is non-zero: it stops at the end index; for each entry it builds a CQE (opcode, qp handle, src qp, wr_id; a fence WQE produces no CQE); for the last WQE, if the hardware status is not OK, it reports an error CQE with the hardware status REGARDLESS of whether that WQE was signalled, consumes one budget unit and calls bnxt_qplib_mark_qp_error(qp); otherwise on chips before gen P5/P7 it runs the legacy 9060 workaround (which may stop the walk by jumping to out with *lib_qp set), and only for a signalled WQE emits an OK CQE and decrements the budget. Each processed WQE advances the hardware consumer and swq_last; with sq->single set it handles only one WQE per call. It stores the advanced CQE pointer in *pcqe. If swq_last has not reached the CQE's index (out of budget, a single-step pass, or the workaround exit) it returns -EAGAIN (so -EAGAIN is not only for budget exhaustion, also for sq->single and the workaround path); otherwise it clears sq->single and returns 0.
note: Reviewers: original right (0 for a flushed QP or a failed slot lookup; -EAGAIN also for sq->single); round 15 right (an error CQE is produced for the last, possibly unsignalled, WQE and the QP is marked in error, 2983-2998). Callees not read.

name: bwi_led_blink_start
prose: Static void (if_bwi.c:3941-3959) that starts blinking the activity LED. It reads the GPIO control register, applies bwi_led_onoff(led, val, 1) to turn the LED on (for an active-low LED, BWI_LED_F_ACTLOW, bwi_led_onoff inverts the request so the GPIO mask bit is CLEARED rather than set, if_bwi.c:3837-3842) and writes the register back. If the LED has the BWI_LED_F_SLOW flag it applies BWI_LED_SLOWDOWN to both on_dur and off_dur, which sets each to (dur * 3) / 2, i.e. lengthens each by about 50 percent (if_bwivar.h:64). It then sets sc_led_blinking = 1, stores off_dur in sc_led_blink_offdur and arms the blink callout to call bwi_led_blink_next(sc) after on_dur ticks. It returns nothing.
note: Reviewers: original right (for ACTLOW LEDs the GPIO bit is cleared, not set); round 15 (SLOWDOWN doubles rather than halves) is also not exact: the macro in if_bwivar.h:64 multiplies by 3/2, so it neither halves nor doubles.

name: bwn_phy_lp_rccal_r12
prose: Static int (if_bwn_phy_lp.c:1813-1930) performing the RC calibration of an LP PHY with an rev 1/2 radio; it returns 0 in every case. It switches to channel 7 (a failure only prints a message and the function continues), saves whether TX override is active (txo) and the current bbmult and, if txo, the TX gain, and saves seven PHY registers (RF_OVERRIDE_0 and _VAL_0, AFE_CTL_OVR and _OVRVAL, RF_OVERRIDE_2 and _2_VAL, LP_PHY_CTL). It turns TX power control off, sets the receiver deaf and the TR switch override and writes a long list of override bits. It runs the loopback measurement (bwn_phy_lp_loopback); if that returns -1 it jumps to done without calibrating. Otherwise it sets the RX gain index and for each capacitor value i in 128..159 writes it to the B2062 RXBB calibration register and, for each of 21 tone frequencies j, turns on the DDFS tone and runs bwn_phy_lp_rx_iq_est: a failed estimate jumps to done (skipping bwn_phy_lp_ddfs_turnoff); otherwise it accumulates the squared difference between the table power and the measured power and stores the best i in plp->plp_rccap. At done it clears the deaf state, masks the RF_OVERRIDE_0 and _2 registers to their low bits, writes back the seven saved registers, restores bbmult, the TX gain (if txo was set) and the TX power control mode, and calls bwn_phy_lp_set_rccap if plp_rccap is non-zero. Registers that were written with fixed values and are not restored: PS_CTL_OVERRIDE_VAL0..2, TX_GAIN_CTL_OVERRIDE_VAL, RX_GAIN_CTL_OVERRIDE_VAL, the RX gain index and the B2062 RXBB calibration register (the last is left at the final probed value unless set_rccap rewrites it).
note: Reviewers: original right (PS_CTL_OVERRIDE_VAL0-2 and the TX/RX gain override values are not restored, 1869-1875); round 15 right that B2062 RF registers are also left modified (1890). Callees not read.
